question: Who was conferred with the Ashok Chakra for his gallantry in 26/11 Mumbai terrorist attacks?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hemant Karkare.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hemant Karkare led the **ATS team** in response to the coordinated terrorist attacks that took place in Mumbai in **November 2008.**
 
• He played a crucial role in neutralizing the terrorists at various locations, including the iconic **Taj Mahal Palace Hotel.**
 
• Tragically, Hemant Karkare** lost his life in the line of duty** during the attacks while fighting against the terrorists.
 
• In recognition of his exceptional bravery and supreme sacrifice, he was posthumously** honoured with the Ashok Chakra**, India's **highest peacetime gallantry award.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohan Chand Sharma:**

 
 
• He was an **Indian Police Service (IPS) officer **serving with the Delhi Police's Special Cell.
 
• He led the operation against terrorists in the **Batla House encounter,** which took place in **Delhi in 2008.**
 
• Sharma displayed exemplary courage and professionalism during the operation, where he lost his life in the line of duty.
 
• In recognition of his bravery and sacrifice in the Batla House encounter, Mohan Chand Sharma was posthumously awarded the **Ashok Chakra**, India's highest peacetime gallantry award.
 
 
 
• **Mohit Sharma:**
 
 
• Major Mohit Sharma, an** Indian Army Officer** from the elite** 1st Para SF,** was posthumously awarded the **Ashoka Chakra**, India's highest peace-time military decoration. 
 
• He engaged in an** encounter with terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir, killing four terrorists and rescuing two teammates** before succumbing to multiple gunshot wounds. 
 
• Major Sharma had previously received two gallantry decorations and was honoured by having a **Delhi Metro station named after him in 2019.**
 
 
 
• **R P Diengdoh:**
 
 
• R P Diengdoh, an Indian Army soldier, was awarded the** Ashok Chakra** for his bravery and sacrifice during an** operation against militants in Jammu and Kashmir in 2018.**
